text:
Ben: hey folks, first-week snag. I can ssh to bastion but cannot reach the internal API gateway (api-internal.svc:443) from my laptop even after connecting the corp VPN. curl just times out. anyone know if onboarding machines get a different split-tunnel profile?
Claire: welcome Ben! quick question: are you on a company laptop or personal? and which VPN client/version?
Ben: company ThinkPad, Ubuntu 22.04, using corp-vpn (wireguard wrapper v1.4). laptop is enrolled in MDM.
Zoe: can you try a raw connect: `nc -vz api-internal.svc 443` from your laptop and then from the bastion?
Ben: laptop:
```
$ nc -vz api-internal.svc 443
nc: connectx to api-internal.svc port 443 (tcp) failed: Operation timed out
```
Ben: bastion:
```
$ nc -vz api-internal.svc 443
Connection to api-internal.svc 443 port [tcp/*] succeeded!
```
Claire: that indicates the service is only reachable via the VPC and your client isn't routing the VPC CIDR over the tunnel. can you paste `ip route` while connected?
Ben: `ip route` shows only my default and my home subnet, no 10.42.0.0/16 or the 172.31.0.0/16 VPCs.
Zoe: onboarding cohort machines are supposed to get a reduced split-tunnel profile (for compliance) that currently only includes corp services. looks like the tag that would add the dev VPCs didn't apply to your laptop. sometimes MDM groups don't sync during provisioning.
Ben: any quick unblock so i can run integration tests?
Claire: easiest short-term: SSH local port forward through bastion: `ssh -L 8443:api-internal.svc:443 ubuntu@bastion.company` then point your curl to `https://localhost:8443` (or set HTTP_PROXY for apps).
Ben: tried forwarding, worked for curl but my dockerized test suite still fails because it resolves the service name before the tunnel and doesn't honor our env proxy.
Zoe: alternative: set up a system-wide SOCKS proxy with `ssh -D 1080 ubuntu@bastion.company -N` and use `socks5h` so DNS resolves over the proxy. On Linux you can run `export ALL_PROXY=socks5h://localhost:1080` and many tools follow it.
Ben: socks approach got the tests green, thanks.
Jordan: (secops) quick heads-up: if infra adds VPC CIDRs or pushes internal DNS to onboarding split-tunnel, SecOps needs to approve because that exposes our internal resolver to remote endpoints. we'll prioritize the review but expect a short questionnaire on approved OS images and MDM enrollment status.
Ben: that makes sense. my laptop is MDM-enrolled and has the standard image. happy to add serial/model to the ticket.
Claire: infra-bot, can you open a ticket to add Ben's machine to the onboarding profile and include a request to push the dev VPC routes + internal DNS for the onboarding cohort? tag SecOps.
infra-bot: Created INFRA-5901: "onboarding: include dev VPCs + internal DNS for onboarding WireGuard profile; verify MDM tags" assigned to @Claire, requested SecOps review (@Jordan). SLA: 72h.
Zoe: if SecOps prefers not to expose resolver, another approved option is to run a bastion-side proxy (short-lived creds) that new hires can use until they pass MDM checks. i'll add that as an option in INFRA-5901.
Ben: fyi my VPN client logs show the server pushing routes but the kernel rejects the add because i already have a broad 10.0.0.0/8 via my home network (weird home router). is there a safe way to add the more specific route manually on Ubuntu?
Claire: yes: `sudo ip route add 10.42.0.0/16 via <wg_gateway>` should work, where `<wg_gateway>` is the interface gateway (check `ip addr`/`wg` output). but if your home router already answers for 10.0.0.0/8 you'll want the more specific /16 so traffic prefers the tunnel. i'll caution to remove the manual route after we fix the profile.
Ben: ok noted. i'll stick to the SSH socks for now and add my laptop details to INFRA-5901. thanks for the quick help and the warm welcome :smile:
Zoe: welcome aboard! ping here if the ticket does not move in 3 days and we'll escalate.
